label: GO: stay with a2 after a fresh common-unrewarded a2->S2 trial
explanation: Fires only at GO steps (zero at D1/D2), and only when the agent is choosing a2 (model_act==2; policy logit a1-a2 mostly between -8.9 and -4.4, a moderate rather than extreme a2 preference). Requires that the previous trial was a2 to S2 (common) and unrewarded (prev_reward 0; essentially never after a reward). It is strongest on the first such loss and much weaker or silent when the trial before that was also an a2/S2-common loss (excluding those raises precision 0.71 to 0.81). So it reads as: agent sticks with a2 despite a fresh common-transition loss. All variables are observed at GO (model_act is the agent's own current choice). Dev: P 0.81, R 0.79, F1 0.80, mass recall 0.83. Most remaining misses are rel -3 GO steps where the previous trial lies outside the window (prev_action unknown); a looser version allowing unknown history reaches mass recall 0.99 but precision 0.60. Never fires on a1 choices, rewarded history, or rare-transition previous trials.

issues: The factual claims hold up. Phase: 100% of the mass is at GO and none at D1 or D2. Choice: (GO & model_act==1) gives 0 actives out of 175k steps. After a reward: (GO & prev_reward==1) has P 0.002 and mass 0.003. After a rare transition: (GO & prev_reward==0 & model_act==2 & prev_common==0) has P 0.002. Repeated losses: the subset where the trial before was also an unrewarded a2/S2-common trial has P 0.137 and mass 0.004, so the 'weaker or silent on repeated losses' claim is right.

One systematic miss class is left. All rel -3 GO steps are missed: 16.5% of the activation mass and 3623 of 21970 actives. The predicate cannot fire there because prev_action == -1 at the window's first trial. The original agent knew about this and kept 'explained' with test F1 0.79, which is below the bar. The gap is fixable: the logit band from its own explanation recovers these steps. At rel -3, (GO & prev_reward==0 & model_act==2 & -9 < choice < -5) has P 0.66, versus P 0.31 without the band.

The in-window false positives are also systematic. Adding choice < -4 to the original predicate raises dev precision from 0.81 to 0.87 with no loss of recall. With -4 < choice < 0 the predicate has P 0.07, so the 'moderate preference for a2' part of the explanation is load-bearing but was left out of the predicate.

Smaller residual pattern: if the agent had just switched to a2 (two trials back it chose a1), the feature is almost silent (P 0.04, n = 630). So it also wants an a2 streak of at least two trials. This is minor.
Precision is lower when S1 is the good state (0.68, versus 0.90 when S2 is good). With choice < -4 this rises to 0.81, so most of the gap is again explained by the logit band.
Future variables: none are used. model_act and choice are the agent's own policy outputs at GO, which the task allows, and the history variables are all observed.
